div.head: V Atr Inscr.
div.ab: In nomine Domini, anno dominicae incarnationis MVIII.
In nomine Domini, anno Dominicae incarnationis MVIII:
Im Namen des Herrn, im Jahre der Fleischwerdung des Herrn 1008. (Vom Beschlusse der Englischen Witan. G2).
In the name of the Lord, in the year of the Lord's incarnation 1008. (Of the decision of the English witan. G2)
In the name of the Lord.
In the name of the Lord, 1008 years since the incarnation of the Lord:
div.note: Base text K = G (Cotton Nero A I f. 89, after III Eg, c. 1060); N = G2 (Cotton Nero A I f. 116v, after a homily attributed to Wulfstan, c. 1070); D (CCCC 201 p. 48) is also given here. Liebermann suggests VI Atr (‘at Enham’) may be a private reworking of the draft of V Atr. G2 inserts and omits matter as in X Atr 1–2.1.; AU: added from Rabin p. None, October 2026 (Rabin’s text); AV: added from Rabin p. None, October 2026 (Rabin’s translation); AY: added from Rabin p. None, October 2026 (Rabin’s note to the text)

Manuscripts: D = Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 201, pp. 48–51; G1 = London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero A.i, fols. 89v–92r; G2 = London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero A.i, fols. 116v–19r.
In . . . MVIII: Be Angolwitena gerednesse G2; In nomine domini D

note.seg: B. A. g. decorated in red.
vielleicht ist VI Atr. ‘zu Enham’ eine private Bearbeitung der Vorlage von V Atr., lautet aber bisweilen weniger ursprünglich als V Atr.
perhaps VI Atr. ‘at Enham’ is a private revision of the exemplar of V Atr., but its wording is sometimes less original than V Atr.
Das Wort, Toller fehlend, erregt kein Bedenken angesichts von Angelcyning, -cynn, -cyrice, -þeod, Angulscaxe
The word, which is missing from Toller, raises no doubts in view of Angelcyning, -cynn, -cyrice, -þeod, Angulscaxe

The difference in the headings as preserved in the three MSS is noticeable. That in G is the fullest and is probably authentic. It is analogous in form to the heading of VIII Atr. and is specially important as giving the date of the ordinance.
The form Angolwitena in G₂ is unusual and is not quoted in BT. Liebermann accepts it as genuine however and parallel to such compounds as Angelcyning, -cynn, -cyrice, -þeod, and Angulseaxe.
